cause: A tab's deterministic query id is reused after closing. Its request generation is also reset to1 because the deleted tab no longer exists. Delayed successes or errors from the closed tab then match the replacement tab's id and generation. A late page2 response can likewise collide once a reopened tab requests its own page2.

proposal: Allocate every SOOP search request's generation from a monotonically increasing ref owned by the mounted SoopDiscovery component. Allocate inside load so initial searches, retries and pagination all receive a fresh identity. Tab deletion never resets this allocator. Keep deterministic query ids for existing-tab selection and keep response checks on both id and generation. Initial tab creation carries an inert generation0 until its synchronously queued load assigns the unique generation.
